name: Seventh Crusade, Death of Louis IX
summary: Louis IX of France leads his second crusade, this time against Tunis, where his army is devastated by dysentery. Louis himself dies of plague, becoming the only French king canonized as a saint. His death effectively ends the era of large royal-led crusades; future efforts are smaller, more commercial, and increasingly ineffective.

_quarry.structural_significance: Louis IX's canonization shapes the idealized image of the Christian king; his death at Tunis ends the Capetian commitment to crusading; the crusading ideal survives but in increasingly theoretical form.
